chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, and someone else, narrated it with an elevated chain (marfu'). He said:

In the Kaaba there used to be two gazelles of gold and five swords. So when Khuza'a overcame Jurhum at the Sanctuary, Jurhum threw the swords and the two gazelles into the well of Zamzam, and threw rocks into it, and filled it up and concealed its traces. So when Qusayy overcame Khuza'a, they did not know the location of Zamzam, and its location was hidden from them.

So when Abdul Muttalib prevailed, and a mat would be spread for him in the courtyard of the Kaaba — something that was not done for anyone else there — while he was sleeping in the shade of the Kaaba, he saw in his dream that a visitor came to him and said: 'Dig Barra.' He said: 'And what is Barra?' Then he came to him on the second day and said: 'Dig Tayba.' Then he came to him on the third day and said: 'Dig al-Masouna.' He said: 'And what is al-Masouna?'

Then he came to him on the fourth day and said: 'Dig Zamzam — it will neither run dry nor be disparaged; it quenches the great pilgrims in the presence of the white-footed crow, by the colony of ants.' And there was a rock near Zamzam from which ants would emerge, and the white-footed crow would alight upon it every day to catch the ants. So when Abdul Muttalib saw this, he recognized the location of Zamzam.

So he said to Quraysh: 'I have been commanded during four nights to dig Zamzam, and it is our heritage and our glory, so come, let us dig it.' But they did not respond to him. So he began digging it by himself, and he had only one son, al-Harith, who used to assist him in the digging.

So when that became difficult for him, he went to the door of the Kaaba, then raised his hands and supplicated to God, Mighty and Majestic, and made a vow to Him that if He were to grant him ten sons, he would sacrifice the most beloved of them to Him as an act of drawing near to God, Mighty and Majestic.

So when he dug and reached the well — the well of Ismail — and knew that he had reached the water, he proclaimed Takbir, and Quraysh proclaimed Takbir. And they said: 'O Abu al-Harith! This is our heritage and we have a share in it.' He said to them: 'You did not assist me in digging it. It belongs to me and my children until the end of eternity.'

key_terms.الطَّوِيّ: A built/lined well, specifically referring to the well Ismail (AS) built
key_terms.الْغُرَابُ الْأَعْصَم: The white-footed crow (white on legs/feet), the identifying sign for locating Zamzam
key_terms.تَقَرُّب: Drawing near to God through acts of worship or sacrifice
key_terms.زَمْزَم: The sacred well within the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, associated with Hajar and Ismail (AS)
key_terms.مَأْثُرَة: Heritage, source of pride, ancestral glory
key_terms.نَذَر: A solemn vow to God to perform an act if a specific condition is met

ai.seo_question: How was the Zamzam well discovered by Abdul Muttalib according to hadith?
ai.summary: This narrative hadith recounts the discovery and excavation of the sacred Zamzam well by Abdul Muttalib, grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW). After the well had been buried and its traces hidden by the tribe of Jurhum when driven out by Khuza'a, Abdul Muttalib was guided to its location through a series of four dream visions over four consecutive nights. The hadith preserves the significant episode of Abdul Muttalib's vow to sacrifice his most beloved son if God granted him ten sons, which later gave rise to the near-sacrifice of Abdullah, the Prophet's father.
